theme: Recovering the sharp event from a blurred trace
title: Calibration Burst — recovering spikes past the noise floor of a triangular blur
strategies: trivial: emit the constant 0 filter (never fires) -> reproduces the checker's all-zero baseline, Ratio ~0.1

greedy: read off the paired calibration burst, run an unregularised ordinary-least-squares fit using the FULL 11-tap window (radius 5) to invert the blur -- the textbook 'just solve for the inverse filter' move; on wide-kernel/ample-data cases it looks fine, but on narrow-kernel/short-burst cases the regression is badly over-parameterised and the fitted taps blow up, amplifying fresh noise on the held-out trace far worse than predicting nothing

strong: first ESTIMATE the kernel's usable support from the calibration cross-correlation between x_cal and y_cal (where the correlation-with-lag drops into the noise floor), then fit a RIDGE-regularised filter restricted to that estimated support with the ridge strength itself chosen by a train/validation split of the calibration burst -- stopping resolution at the estimated noise floor instead of maximising in-sample sharpness

headroom above strong: a smarter noise-floor estimator (matched-filter energy test instead of a fixed threshold) and per-tap shrinkage instead of a single ridge scalar would push held-out MSE further toward the irreducible sensor-noise floor
